text: Year 3594, autumn. The door is open. I want that written down plainly, because I have spent five waves and two thousand years being wrong about this world and today the arithmetic finally came back on my side. When I taxed the traits last turn, prey defence stood at 1.47 and the reliable-kill bar at 1.89 against a genome that can express 1.60 -- a shut door. Seven hundred years of paying for armour has brought defence to 0.98 and the bar to 1.36, and it has held there across the last nine thousand ticks rather than continuing to fall, which tells me this is not a slope I am riding down but the floor the world has settled on. A margin of 0.24 under the ceiling is what I get, and it is not going to get better by waiting another turn. The stagnation warning has cleared itself on the way, exactly as I guessed it would: variance was flat because nothing cost anything, and now that armour has a price the genome has something to argue about again. So the hunters go in. But not the hunters I sent the last five times, because I have finally understood that the bar was only half of what killed them. A hand-seeded founder wakes with an untaught brain and one unit of energy, pushing about two-thirds of its nominal power with roughly two hundred and fifty ticks of fuel to find its first kill -- and every one of my previous stocks was a pure carnivore at diet 0.95, which is to say every one of them was an animal that had to solve hunting, from scratch, blind, before it starved. Five times I sent an animal on a errand it had one chance at. This stock does not have to. Diet 0.55 makes them omnivores: they can stand in the grass and eat the grass while their brains learn the country, and the grass is not scarce -- flora is at seven and a half thousand with three tenths of the world under cover. carrion_gut at 0.9 means they digest meat properly anyway, so a kill or a corpse pays them full price without their needing a carnivore's gut. And they are armed for the bar that actually exists: fangs 1.0 on a frame of 0.5 is 1.30, shear_tooth at 0.9 adds another 1.03, which is 2.33 nominal and 1.56 after the founder's derating -- fourteen per cent over a bar of 1.36, where the last wave was thirteen per cent under it. I have also stripped their armour to 0.12 on purpose. Nothing in Primordia hunts a predator, so armour is pure tax now that trait_cost_scale is 0.5, and the tax is the thing I am trying to spend on metabolism instead. This has the pleasant side effect of answering the only warning the world is still raising: the omnivores are down to four, and have been guttering for years, and this is a founder stock for them as much as it is a wedge for a food chain. Four hundred and fifty of them into the coastal plain at (170,170), where three animals in four live. What I read next turn is not the carnivore count and not even the omnivore count -- it is diet_mean in the survivors and shear_tooth's split. If diet climbs off 0.55 in anything, the world has re-invented carnivory for itself and I can stop hand-feeding it. If shear_tooth splits at last -- climbing where diet climbs, stripped where it does not -- then Primordia has a food chain for the first time since the nineteen-hundreds. And if this wave dies too, then the fault was never the bar or the brains or the diet, and I will stop seeding predators and say so in this Chronicle instead of trying a seventh time.
